newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom, Kirch, CLT/Ufa in digital TV deal.
newsitem.headline: Telekom, Kirch, CLT/Ufa in digital TV deal.

text.p: German phone giant Deutsche Telekom AG said on Wednesday it has reach an agreement with Bavarian medial mogul Leo Kirch and the CLT/Ufa broadcasting group to launch digital television in Germany.

As part of the deal the three companies will hold equal stakes in Beta Research GmbH, the Kirch Group unit that developed the basic digital decoder technology, and use Kirch's "d-box" decoder. Telekom will also raise cable subscription fees by 15 percent to 25.90 marks a month in the autumn.
"CLT/Ufa and the Kirch Group have reached an agreement with Deutsche Telekom on the basic outline for opening the digital television market," Telekom said in a regulatory statement.

"The agreement should create the foundation for the accelerated development of the digital television market that will create new opportunities for programme providers that want to become active on the digital market."
The deal will probably get a close look by anti-trust officials, who have already blocked two previous attempts by the Telekom, Bertelsmann and Kirch to form a joint venture in digital television.

It follows a previous announcement by Kirch and Bertelsmann that they had agreed to work together in digital TV and, if successful, it would end two years of wrangling over which basic decoder technology would be used in Germany.

The new digital decoder will replace the analog pay TV decoder used by Germany's leading pay TV group, Premiere, and become the only decoder used in Germany for pay TV programming via cable or satellite.

Deutsche Telekom said it would use the conditional access system -- the core technology that allows individual billing for programming -- developed by Beta Research and Telekom would provide its cable customers with an electronic programme guide.
